unsettled: NO ROWS RECORDED, because the official national list could not be read online. The DRC classes its controlled substances in tables annexed to a Ministry of Health order: Arrêté ministériel n°1250/CAB/MIN/S/0002/DC/OWE/2021 (27 February 2021), as modified and completed by Arrêté ministériel n°1250/CAB/MIN/SPHP/038/DCA/CPh/2022 (24 November 2022). Art. 83 of the 2022 text says the substances 'sont classés dans les tableaux I, II et III, en annexe' (are classed in Tables I, II and III, annexed). No copy found online reproduces that annex. The two copies of the 2022 text (leganet.be; droitcongolais.info) and the one copy of the 2021 text (droitcongolais.info) all end at the signature, and none of these hosts is a government site. The regulator ACOREP's own copy of the 2021 order (acorep-dpmrdc.org) no longer loads, its web-archive copy is blocked to WebFetch, and ACOREP's current site shows 'Pas de publication' in its legal library. The Journal officiel's own site sells issues and gives no free text. So no list entry was read, no item was matched, and nothing was guessed.

All 77 items are unread, so none is recorded as 'not found' (not_found is empty). By drug page: 2c-x (2C-B, 2C-I, 2C-E, 2C-C, 2C-T-7); 5-meo-dmt (5-MeO-DMT); amphetamine (amfetamine, dexamfetamine, lisdexamfetamine); benzodiazepines (diazepam, alprazolam, clonazepam, lorazepam, bromazepam, etizolam, flualprazolam, flubromazolam); cannabis (cannabis and cannabis resin, delta-9-THC (dronabinol), CBD); cocaine (cocaine, coca leaf); dmt-ayahuasca (DMT; ayahuasca, if named); dxm (dextromethorphan); fentanyl-and-analogues (fentanyl, carfentanil, acetylfentanyl, furanylfentanyl, sufentanil, remifentanil); ghb-gbl (GHB, GBL, 1,4-butanediol); heroin (heroin); ketamine (ketamine, esketamine); kratom (Mitragyna speciosa, mitragynine, 7-hydroxymitragynine); lsd (LSD); mdma (MDMA, MDA, MDEA); mescaline (mescaline; peyote or San Pedro, if named); methadone-buprenorphine (methadone, buprenorphine); methamphetamine (methamphetamine); methylphenidate (methylphenidate); pcp (PCP); prescription-opioids (morphine, oxycodone, hydrocodone, codeine, tramadol, tapentadol); psilocybin (psilocybin, psilocin); salvia-divinorum (Salvia divinorum, salvinorin A); synthetic-cannabinoids (JWH-018, AM-2201, 5F-MDMB-PINACA, MDMB-4en-PINACA, ADB-BUTINACA); synthetic-cathinones (cathinone, cathine, mephedrone, MDPV, alpha-PVP, 3-MMC, 3-CMC, 4-CMC, NEP, 2-MMC, 4-BMC).

Generic clause (editor's decision). Art. 84 of the 2022 text says that all plants and substances 'classées comme stupéfiants ou psychotropes par les Conventions internationales' (classified as narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances by the international conventions), or classified under them, their preparations, and other plants and substances dangerous to public health 'sont inscrites à l'un des trois tableaux suivants' (are entered in one of the following three tables). Read literally, every substance in the UN schedules is on one of the national tables, but which table cannot be known without the annex. Art. 3 adds that the tables may be 'modifiées de temps à autre conformément à l'article 3 de la Convention unique de 1961' (amended from time to time under article 3 of the 1961 Single Convention), and art. 87 that 'L'Acorep peut modifier les tableaux' (ACOREP may modify the tables). No modification by ACOREP was found, and whether the annex keeps up with UN scheduling after 2022 is not known. No 'covered by reference' rows were made (as was done for Nigeria's NDLEA Act s. 52), because the instruction for this country was to record no rows without a readable official list, and because the clause was read only on non-government hosts.

The three tables, as art. 84 of the 2022 text describes them: Tableau I 'plantes et substances à haut risque dépourvues d'intérêt en médecine' (high-risk plants and substances of no medical value); Tableau II, high risk and of medical value; Tableau III, 'à risque' (at risk) and of medical value. Art. 87: 'Les préparations contenant une substance inscrite au tableau I sont prohibées' (preparations containing a Table I substance are prohibited). Art. 3 defines 'Tableaux I, II, III et IV', but arts. 83 and 84 set up three tables; the text read does not explain a fourth.

Cannabis (editor's decision). The body of the 2022 text defines 'Cannabis' (the flowering or fruiting tops), 'Plante de cannabis' (any plant of the genus) and 'Résine de cannabis' (art. 3). Art. 100, in its chapter on cannabis for medical and scientific use, allows medical cultivation of varieties with THC 'inférieures ou égales à 0,2%' (at or below 0.2%) and high in CBD. The 1903 ordinance-law bans 'La culture, la vente, le transport et la détention du chanvre à fumer' (the cultivation, sale, transport and possession of smoking hemp), and also its use, smoked or consumed in any other way (art. 1); whether it is still in force was not established. Neither text is a list, and both were read only on non-government hosts. No cannabis row was made, and the table placement of cannabis, THC and CBD is unknown.

Where the annex may be found (to settle). Leganet's table of contents lists the 2022 order in the Journal officiel, numéro spécial, 6 March 2023, from col. 35, with the next text at col. 87; whether the annex is printed in those columns is not known. The Journal officiel sells issues at journalofficiel.cd. No Journal officiel issue publishing the 2021 order was found (Leganet's tables of contents for 11 issues from 15 March to 15 December 2021 were checked; not every issue has one). The annexed Tableaux I to III are needed, from that issue or from ACOREP, before any DRC row can be made.

No national drug law with its own schedule was found. Neither order's preamble cites a national narcotics law: the 2021 order cites the 1961 Single Convention, and the 2022 order the 1961 and 1971 Conventions, with the 1933 pharmacy ordinance (Ordonnance n°27bis/Hyg. du 15 mars 1933) and Law n°18/035 of 13 December 2018 on public health. droitcongolais.info files only the 1903 ordinance-law under '325 Stupéfiants'. A commercial website names an 'Ordonnance-loi N° 71-079 du 26 mars 1971 sur les stupéfiants'; no official or legal-database copy of such a text was found, so it is unverified and nothing was taken from it.

The essential-medicines list on ACOREP's site (LNME, édition 2020, 'RÉVISION OCTOBRE 2020') marks no control status; its heading '27.1. PSYCHOTROPES' is a therapeutic group. It is not a controlled-substances list and gave no row. Until the annex is read, the DRC has no national rows: the drug pages keep only the UN treaty layer, and the merge script reads this file as 0 rows on 0 drug pages.
